fields.prompt: Transcribe the exact text of the piece's <h1> headline, verbatim, in quotation marks.
State specifically what the chart marks show (direction, magnitude, or pattern) and whether that matches the headline's claim. Cite the visual evidence itself, not a restatement of the headline.
Cite the visible axis domain(s) exactly as rendered from the tick labels (e.g. "x: 1958-2026, y: 303-430 ppm"). Read the labels; do not estimate.
List every distinct hex color you can identify in the piece as rendered (marks, emphasis, text, background), as a list of hex codes.
Count the number of distinct data series/lines/mark-groups visible in the piece. Report as an integer.
Name the ONE emphasis color used in the piece (its hex code) and state exactly where it appears (which mark, label, or element).
Transcribe the exact 'Source:' attribution line verbatim, in quotation marks.
Looking only at the still poster frame (as if motion never plays), state exactly what finding is legible and what, if anything, would be lost without the animation.

Name or quote the specific data-state change the motion encodes (e.g. "line extends left-to-right as year advances 1958-2026"). If the motion is decorative only and encodes no data-state change, state that explicitly — this is a VIOLATION condition.
